title: M&S Wants to Give 1,000 Young People a Career Boost!
summary: Have you ever worried about finding a good job when you grow up? You’re not alone. Right now, lots of young people in the UK are struggling to get their first job. In fact, experts say one in six young people could be out of school and out of work in five years if nothing changes. That’s why Marks & Spencer (M&S), the big store chain, is stepping up. They’re launching a brand-new training program for 1,000 young people aged 16 to 24. Over the next 18 months, these trainees will get paid while they learn all about working in retail—that’s jobs in stores, like helping customers and managing products. The best part? If you do well, you can get more training to become a store manager. And you don’t need a college degree! “We want more young people to see retail not just as a first job, but as a career with real opportunity,” said Thinus Keeve, an M&S director. This comes at a time when many entry-level jobs are disappearing, partly because of new technology like AI. The government is also working on plans to help young people get tech skills. So if you’re dreaming of a job where you can grow, M&S might just have a spot for you.
why_it_matters: Thinking about your future career early can help you find opportunities, just like these training programs prepare young people for jobs.
